official.status_note: The official site states: 'We are no longer accepting applications for the Vanier Canada Graduate Scholarships. Please refer to the Canada Graduate Research Scholarship - Doctoral program web page for information regarding the new harmonized program.'
benefits: Valued at $50,000 per year for three years during doctoral studies
eligibility: Candidates must be nominated by a Canadian institution holding a Vanier quota
Citizenship: Canadian citizens, permanent residents of Canada, or foreign citizens
Areas of research: health research, natural sciences and/or engineering, or social sciences and humanities
requirements: Candidates should seek a nomination only from the institution at which they want to study
coverage: $50,000 per year for three years during doctoral studies
application_method: Gain admission to a doctoral programme at a Canadian institution
Seek the institution's internal nomination; the institution forwards the candidate to the national competition within its quota
official.application_route: Institution nomination only - candidates cannot apply directly
official.citizenship_residency: Canadian citizens, permanent residents of Canada and foreign citizens are all eligible
official.international_eligibility: Yes - foreign citizens are explicitly listed as eligible
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Health research, natural sciences and/or engineering, social sciences and humanities
official.duration: Three years at $50,000 per year during doctoral studies
official.description: Named after Major-General Georges P. Vanier, the Vanier Canada Graduate Scholarships program helps Canadian institutions attract highly qualified doctoral students, and is jointly administered by CIHR, NSERC and SSHRC.

verification.notes: The official Vanier site was fetched live; the $50,000 per year value, selection criteria and nomination requirement are confirmed, and the homepage itself announces that the programme no longer accepts applications and points to the harmonized Canada Graduate Research Scholarship - Doctoral programme.

applicant_utility.summary: Read the first line of the official homepage before anything else: Vanier is no longer accepting applications, and the tri-agencies now run doctoral funding through the harmonized Canada Graduate Research Scholarship - Doctoral programme instead. If you are building a Canadian PhD funding plan in this cycle, direct your effort at CGRS-D and your target university's internal nomination process. The $50,000-per-year figure remains useful only as historical context for what Vanier awarded and as a benchmark when comparing current university packages.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Historically, doctoral students whom a Canadian institution chose to nominate; the live successor route is now CGRS-D.
application_readiness_checklist: Open the Canada Graduate Research Scholarship - Doctoral page on NSERC's site and re-target your plan there
Ask prospective supervisors whether their department submits internal nominations and by what internal date
Keep evidence of academic excellence, research potential and leadership ready - the old Vanier weighting is the best preview of how the harmonized programme assesses candidates
Check that your university holds a quota before scheduling around national dates
common_rejection_risks: Applying directly as an individual - Vanier-style awards require the institution to nominate
Relying on third-party listings that still describe the programme as open
Confusing the closed federal award with university-funded doctoral packages
document_audit: The institution handles nomination, so the real gate is your department's internal deadline, which sits well before any national date
alerts: Vanier CGS no longer accepts applications - any page still soliciting them is out of date
The successor CGRS-D may carry different values and rules; verify them there rather than relying on the $50,000 figure
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Institution-nominated only; with Vanier closed, the equivalent route is the harmonized CGRS-D applied for through the Canadian institution.
